Kansas property tax is assessed and collected at the local level, and owners can appeal an assessment.

What the official sources say

  • Taxpayer may appeal to the county appraiser within 30 days of the mailing date of the notice of value. (Equalization Appeal Process for Real Property (K.S.A. 79-1448); source)
  • Informal hearings must be held by May 15 and results mailed by May 20. (Equalization Appeal Process for Real Property (K.S.A. 79-1496); source)
  • After the supplemental notice of final value, the taxpayer may appeal to BOTA within 30 days of its mailing date. (Equalization Appeal Process for Real Property (K.S.A. 79-1496); source)
  • Petition for reconsideration of a BOTA decision must be filed with BOTA within 15 days; judicial review in district court within 30 days. (Equalization Appeal Process for Real Property (K.S.A. 74-2426, 77-601 et seq.); source)
  • Residential property is assessed at 11.5% of appraised value. (Slide 6: Kansas Property Classification System; source)
  • A taxpayer must choose one appeal path for the same tax year: appeal at valuation notice (equalization) or pay under protest (K.S.A. 79-2005), not both. (Slide 14: Kansas Provides Appeal Rights; source)
  • BOTA has a Small Claims Division for most residential and smaller-value commercial properties. (Slide 14: Kansas Provides Appeal Rights; source)
  • Redemption period for real estate bid off by the county is 2 years (1 year for abandoned structures; 3 years for homesteads and other real estate). (K.S.A. 79-2401a; source)
  • Redeeming party pays the sale amount plus accrued interest, delinquent taxes and special assessments, and costs of sale and redemption. (K.S.A. 79-2401a(a); source)

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Kansas offers property tax relief for qualifying homeowners, and official sources explain the rules.

What the official sources say

  • Kansas Constitution Art. 15 s.9 exempts from forced sale a homestead of up to 160 acres of farm land or one acre within an incorporated city, occupied as a residence by the owner's family. (Kansas Constitution Art. 15, s. 9; source)
  • The constitutional homestead is not exempt from sale for taxes or for obligations contracted to purchase the premises or erect improvements. (Kansas Constitution Art. 15, s. 9; source)
  • Kansas offers a homestead property tax refund (Form K-40H) rather than a property tax exemption; 2025 maximum refund is $700. (Homestead or Property Tax Refund for Homeowners - 2025; source)
  • 2025 K-40H eligibility: household income of $43,389 or less and born before Jan 1, 1970, or blind/disabled, or with a qualifying dependent child. (Homestead or Property Tax Refund for Homeowners - 2025; source)
  • K-40PT (age 65+, household income $25,380 or less) refunds property tax; K-40SVR income limit is $58,041. (Homestead or Property Tax Refund for Homeowners - 2025; source)
  • 2025 claims are filed after Dec 31, 2025 and no later than April 15, 2026. (Homestead or Property Tax Refund for Homeowners - 2025; source)
  • First $75,000 of appraised value of residential property is exempt from the statewide school finance mill levy (as of 2024). (Kansas Property Tax Exemptions (KDOR); source)

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Kansas evictions follow notice and court steps set by state law.

What the official sources say

  • Landlord may terminate for unpaid rent after written notice and 3 days (three consecutive 24-hour periods); mailing adds 2 days. (K.S.A. 58-2564(b); source)
  • For material noncompliance, written notice terminates the agreement not less than 30 days after receipt if not remedied in 14 days. (K.S.A. 58-2564(a); source)
  • Landlord files a petition; hearing is set within 3 to 14 days of filing. (Housing - Kansas Self-Help; source)
  • If the tenant contests, a bench trial is set within 14 days of the hearing date. (Housing - Kansas Self-Help; source)
  • A granted eviction produces a writ of restitution executed within 14 days; the court process can take up to 42 days. (Housing - Kansas Self-Help; source)
  • A landlord who conveys premises in a good-faith sale to a bona fide purchaser is relieved of liability under the rental agreement after written notice to the tenant of the conveyance. (K.S.A. 58-2554(a); source)
  • The seller landlord remains liable for any security deposit the tenant is entitled to. (K.S.A. 58-2554(a); source)

A Kansas deed is recorded with the county office named in the sources below.

What the official sources say

  • A conveyance worded 'A.B. quitclaims to C.D.' with description and consideration, signed and acknowledged by the grantor, is a good and sufficient quitclaim conveyance. (K.S.A. 58-2204; source)
  • A sales validation questionnaire must accompany any deed transferring title when recorded, unless an exemption applies. (K.S.A. 79-1437c; source)
  • Recording fees under K.S.A. 28-115 apply. (K.S.A. 28-115; source)
  • Register of deeds in each county records deeds; fees are due before recording. (K.S.A. 28-115(g); source)
  • Since Jan 1, 2018: $17 first page and $13 each additional page for deeds and mortgages, plus $3 per page additional fee under 28-115(b) and $1 per page under (i). (K.S.A. 28-115; source)
  • $1 extra if signer or notary names are not plainly typed or printed under signatures. (K.S.A. 28-115(d); source)

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

This guide covers what official sources say about Kansas transfer on death deeds.

What the official sources say

  • An interest in real estate may be titled in TOD form by recording a deed signed by the record owner naming grantee beneficiaries; no consideration needed. (K.S.A. 59-3501(a); source)
  • Beneficiary signature, consent or notice is not required during the owner's lifetime. (K.S.A. 59-3501(b); source)
  • The deed must be executed, acknowledged and recorded with the register of deeds in the county where the land lies before the owner's death. (K.S.A. 59-3502; source)
  • The statutory form states the deed is revocable and transfers no ownership until the owner's death. (K.S.A. 59-3502; source)
  • Small estate affidavit (K.S.A. 59-1507b) allows transfer of personal property without letters if probate assets do not exceed $75,000. (K.S.A. 59-1507b; source)
  • The statute text covers transfer of personal property; it does not by itself transfer title to real estate. (K.S.A. 59-1507b; source)
